image_description: A realistic photograph of a grey whale surfacing in dark blue ocean water. The image captures the dorsal side of the whale, showing its mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches and a series of dorsal knuckles (humps) along the back where a dorsal fin would typically be. The head is partially visible on the left, and the body extends towards the right, blending into the waves.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is partially submerged and viewed from a high angle; the rostrum shape and blowholes are not clearly visible due to water distortion and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white irregular patches consistent with barnacle infestations.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no triangular dorsal fin. Instead, a series of small humps (knuckles) are visible along the ridge of the back, which is a key identifier for grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body appears thick and robust, consistent with the massive scale of a baleen whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the body skin exhibits the correct texture and coloration patterns.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and underwater; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located on the underside/lateral sides and are completely submerged/occluded in this dorsal view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail section is either out of frame or obscured by the water surface and distance; the flukes are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface texture appears uneven and rough, consistent with the presence of callosities and barnacles described in the taxonomy.
